description: I'm Seif Ashraf, a student interested in planetary science, technology, and research. I'm building a multidisciplinary team to tackle a challenge involving the Moon or Mars. I'm seeking members skilled in programming, data analysis, AI, engineering, and planetary science. I value curiosity, teamwork, and problem-solving. Together, we'll combine our strengths, share ideas, and develop a practical, scientifically sound solution while learning from one another where every contribution matters.
summary:
Earth Analog Finder project is an interactive website that compare desired Earth locations according to similar locations on Moon or Mars according to various conditions like moisture, roughness, mean temperature and other.
The website is built on a simple database that gather different characteristics and pieces of information for many various areas and compares regarding similar places on Earth. In addition to the ability to adjust the factors manually and match the new inputs with a similar area.
For example, the website originally used Kamil Carter in Egypt as a similar refrence on Earth for Shackleton Rim in Moon and Aristarchus Crater in Mars due to the geological formation history.
Our project addresses the challenge of finding suitable locations for future missions on Moon or Mars as it can serve for analogs by discovering new locations on Earth. Moreover, exploring their conditions and supporting scientific researches that can be occured for these places geologically and astronomically. It can improve future mission preperations and facing challenges related to Moon or Mars.
details: The project compares two sites: one on Earth and the other on Mars or the Moon. The project is a website that allows users to add factors such as moisture and temperature. The comparison factors can be added to the website from trusted sources such as the NASA website. The website performs the calculation and provides the similarity score between the two sites. This similarity can assist in training astronauts for their trip to the Moon or testing a rover in similar conditions. The benefits of the project are that it has built-in data for the most common sites, and the website can be used with any provided data. The tools used to make this website are HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The code is built entirely in a single HTML file in order to avoid problems when running the code due to missing files or errors. This idea is creative because it not only compares two places, but also has the ability to compare many places based purely on their conditions.
